question: Who among the following was the first Indian Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CD Deshmukh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **CD Deshmukh** was the first Indian Governor of the Reserve Bank of India.
 
• He served as the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India from **August 11, 1943, to June 30, 1949**.
 
• CD Deshmukh played a significant role in the establishment of the Indian financial system post-independence.
 
• He was also involved in the negotiations for the Bretton Woods Agreement, which led to the establishment of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank.
 
• After his tenure at the RBI, CD Deshmukh went on to serve as India’s Finance Minister from 1950 to 1956.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the central banking institution of India, which controls the issuance and supply of the Indian rupee and manages the country’s main payment systems.
 
• The RBI was established on **April 1, 1935**, during the British Rule in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The RBI plays a crucial role in the development strategy of the Government of India, including maintaining monetary stability in the country.
 
• The headquarters of the Reserve Bank of India is located in Mumbai, Maharashtra.
 
• The RBI’s functions include regulating the issue of banknotes, maintaining reserves to secure monetary stability, and operating the credit and currency system of the country to its advantage.
